questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The aspects of my choice that was most important was to live in a city with a lot of possibilities for things to do besides your studies. Here I chose University of Zurich because it also enabled me to during the weekends to go on hikes and ski trips. For my destination it was also important that I lived in a place where I could feel comfortable but still experience a lot of different cultures and new experiences, and therefore Zurich suited this really well because it is a very international city with a lot of exchange students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have never regretted making the choice of going abroad, it has been one of the best decisions for my own personal well-being and for the experience of going somewhere else while still learning and progressing in your career.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it was quite difficult, especially with regards to when you had to upload wishes/proposals for which courses you were gonna take at the host university because it was really difficult to find the correct courses that I could apply for as an international student. Apart from that it was a nice experience with UCPH providing us with the necessary information and the same thing with UZH providing us with information, e.g. with regards to applying for student accommodation

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had both a mandatory introduction that applied to all international students where they told us about e.g. how to apply for a residence permit, insurances, how to use public transport and different social and study-related activities. As law students we also had a specific mandatory introduction where they told us more about the teachings at the faculty of law, and how you applied for courses with the different deadlines and how the exams functioned.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it was great that they made these introductions mandatory because I could imagine that people otherwise would skip them.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy because UZH and ETH (the two universities in Zurich) both have a partnership with the housing office called WOKO who has a lot of different housing offers. The universities recommended us to apply for this, and I have not regretted signing up for this because it enabled me to get to know a lot of people really quickly - I lived with 14 other people on my floor that I shared a kitchen and bathrooms with. It was also nice to apply for housing through this because it then made the process more smoothly since I did not have to spend a lot of time searching up apartments on the private market with the risk of getting scammed, and the rooms were also quite affordable compared to private rooms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you apply for a WOKO apartment you should bear in mind that these apartments are located a bit outside central Zurich and away from the main building of the universities (around 30 minutes away with public transport). But I figured that this was not a problem since almost all exchange students live at these apartments and therefore everyone is in the same boat and then you can also take the bus together to school

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you apply for student accommodation just remember that you share a lot of things with other people, while this sometimes is a bit annoying with people being a little dirty at times, it is also really rewarding because I lived with people from all across the world and from almost all continents of the world which I found very enriching. A limitation for this WOKO option is also I believe you can at max be 27 years old.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Went very smooth

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just had to upload your personal data and had to provide them with different documents. I then afterwards checked which courses were available for me and got these pre approved at my home institution in order for me to able to apply for these at the host institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I actually don't really know since I didn't make use of any help offered

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This went really well, but the good thing about going on exchange in Zurich is that you are not bound initially by your choice of courses since the deadline of which courses you want to have is first 3-4 weeks in to the semester. This means that in the first couple of weeks you can go around to different classes and test out different courses to see which one you prefer and find the most interesting. That way you can also coordinate a little more with other people if you want to have the same courses, and you also find out a little bit more about what kind of exam the different courses have. UZH offers mobility exams which are exams that can be taken remotely and are oral, and I primarily took courses where this was an option since I prefer oral exams over written ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get pre approved all the courses you find interesting by your home university so that you are able to have them in your learning agreement that you have to make while you are on exchange so that your credits can be transferred. Go a little around and try out different classes - I think I tried out 8-9 classes before I decided on which 5 classes I wanted to have.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were a little more easy than others. I had some courses where there was a lot of reading material bearing in mind that it was only a 6 ECTS course, but then I also had courses where the only material for the exam was the powerpoints and what the professor had said at the lectures. The good thing is that the majority of the courses are being recorded and you can therefore watch them back. All of my courses there were no attendance requirements which meant that your participation in class didn't count in your grade, some classes count participation in their grading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was only lectures and very one-sided in the sense that it was the professor explaining the stuff and us taking notes to what they said. There was not that much interaction, only a few times where the professor would ask small questions to the audience. In many of the classes the professor also did not provide with any reading material or only gave us additional/recommended material if we wanted to add on to the things they told at the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Internet Law (6 ECTS), European Economic Law (6 ECTS), International Financial Law (6 ECTS), Introduction to U.S. Business Law (6 ECTS) and Introduction to Sports Law (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the ones in English because from personal experience the ones taught in German can be very hard to follow along in, and you cannot be sure that they will speak a little Swiss-German in them which is very different to the standard High-German that you learn in school. I would also recommend taking some of the courses that focus on the international or EU aspects of law, or explaining the fundamental principles of a certain law area because that would be more relevant for you in your future rather than learning about some niche Swiss legislation.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When you arrive you have to pay around 60 CHF for a residence permit. You also need to pay for specific trash bags that cost 16 CHF for 10 bags because you cannot just use normal trash bags.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive to go to restaurants, and therefore I have not really been out to eat while being here. Everything that involves a service is quite expensive because the minimum wage in Switzerland is quite high. The groceries are not that much more expensive than Denmark, maybe on average 10% if you just go to Lidl or Aldi.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You get a free gym membership when you are an exchange student, and the university offers a lot of different sporting activities that you for free can sign up for.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university through something called ASVZ offers a lot of sporting activities, e.g. badminton, spinning, yoga, paddle and much more. There is also a lot of different sporting associations that do a lot of different things, but I have not attended any of this. ESN Zurich also offers a lot of fun stuff where I for instance went on a skiing trip, paragliding, and bar crawl, and they do a lot of different things.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on skiing trips around the country or Austria, there is a lot of options that are only 1-2 hours away (Engelberg, Pizol, Arosa, Andermatt, Lax, Davos, St. Anton), so you can easily do it in a day-trip if you want to. When the weather is a bit more nice do hiking trips (Grindelwald, Brienz, Lauterbrunnen, Mürren, Thun, Stoos, Grosser Mythen, Seealpsee, Mount Pilatus). Otherwise visit some of the nice cities around in Switzerland (Luzern, Thun, Basel, Chur, Lausanne, Geneve). If you are in Zurich go and take a swim in Limmat, or if you want to go out go to Langstrasse.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I also went on a trip to Italy in Milano, Como and Lugano for my easter break, which is a big recommendation. You can also easily go to other countries if you want to, e.g. France, Austria, Spain, Netherlands, but I just did not have that as my priority.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is very similar to the lifestyle of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I actually do not really know since I do not know any Swiss students and have not really got to learn any, but I would imagine attending some events of the student associations for instance.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not really any cultural differences I found challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People can be a little reserved but if you just first start talking to them they are very nice and talkative.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for a student accommodation (WOKO) - it will make it so much easier for you to get to know people and attend social events.
Apply for the mobility exam courses - they are a little easier to pass and you will both be with Swiss and exchange students in these classes
Do not expect the semester to just be a piece of cake, I would say it is definitely easier than in Copenhagen, also because the grades do not matter, but the exams are not just you presenting a powerpoint that you made the night before

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a very big exchange student community since the two universities (UZH and ETH) are located right next to each other, and both of them accept a lot of foreign students

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Even though it has been great attending UZH, the best part has no doubt been to get to know a lot of people from around the world. That is also what I loved about my exchange is that it is not the most popular destination for Danish law students at least, and therefore I got to know so many people from around the world, even though in the end I ended up hanging out the most with people from Sweden and Norway

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I have not been away for such a long period before in my life from my family and friends, but even though I sometimes missed them there was also so much going on at your exchange that you at some points would "forget" it a bit because the days just went by so fast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
